start.text: Welcome to station two! This is our UltiMaker S-series printer with the Air Manager.

main2.text: One useful feature of this printer is dual extrusion. It can print using two compatible materials.

choices.label: Why would you need two materials?

main3.text: That flexibility helps when different projects have different requirements. You can choose materials based on what the part needs.

choices.label: How do you choose a material?

main4.text: The Air Manager also creates a more enclosed printing area. It filters air while the printer is operating.

main5.text: So this printer is really about versatility. It gives students another way to approach different design problems.

choices.label: How is this different from the Bambu?

main6.text: That's station two! When you're ready, look for number three to learn about the next printer.

choices.label: Tell me about dual extrusion again.

air_manager.text: That's the Air Manager. It encloses the build area and filters air while the printer is running.

air_manager_benefit.text: The enclosure helps create a more controlled printing environment. The filtration system also helps manage particles from printing.

dual_extrusion.text: Dual extrusion means the printer has two print cores. That lets it use two compatible materials in one print.

choices.label: What else would you use that for?

two_colors.text: It can be used for certain multi-color prints. But the second material can also have a functional purpose.

support.text: One material can build the part while another provides support. Supports help print overhangs and complex shapes.

support_explanation.text: Think of supports as temporary scaffolding for the print. They hold up areas that can't print properly on their own.

support_removal.text: That depends on the material. Some supports can be removed manually, while compatible soluble supports can be dissolved.

cleaner_tease.text: Yep! There's actually another station in this room that demonstrates that post-processing step.

cleaner_tease2.text: You'll get to it later in the tour. Keep following the numbered stations and I'll explain it there.

materials.text: Engineers choose materials based on what the part needs to do. Strength, flexibility, and other properties can all matter.

materials_importance.text: A good shape isn't enough if the material can't do the job. Material selection is an important part of engineering design.

bambu_comparison.text: Both are useful printers, but they offer different workflows and features. The best choice depends on what the project needs.

bye.text: Sounds good! Keep following the numbered stations when you're ready to continue the 3D printing tour.
